Littler's in ridiculous form. He just lifted the World Matchplay, beating Gerwyn Price 18-9 in the final after seeing off Josh Rock and Nathan Aspinall along the way. Backing him short again carries the obvious price risk, given how far ahead of the market he's currently running.

Luke Littler is the projected winner in the PDC World Championship 2027. Due to his determination and resilience, he has risen rapidly through the ranks to become PDC Premier League Champion. He will also win this tournament.

The Nuke won the World Championship in January to become a back-to-back world champion. He has collected all the major honours in the game now. I think his goal will be to achieve a hat trick of World Championship titles. My tip is Luke Littler wins at Alexandra Palace to regain his crown.

The Nuke has won the last two PDC World Championships, and he goes in search of three in a row and a historic hat trick. Littler has reached the final the last three years at the Ally Pally, and I fancy he won't be stopped from becoming a three-time, back-to-back world champion.
Luke Humphries' recent US Masters victory over Littler proves he is the only rival capable of halting the champion's historic run.

Gian van Veen reached the final last year, and those were the first matches he won in the World Championship at Alexandra Palace. I think, much like Luke Littler??'who lost in the final and then came back the next year to win it??'Gian can do the same and become world champion.
Gian van Veen was last year's runner-up who reached the final on his debut. His composure in big matches and consistency at Ally Pally make him a solid e/w punt.

Veen to win the tournament stands as a strong angle because his rising scoring power, calmer doubling under pressure, and improving match-to-match consistency position him as one of the few players capable of sustaining the long-format intensity required to lift the 2027 World title.

After his European regaining of the title, I expect him to make the final of the PDC World Championship. 25/1 is a steal.

The 2022 champion returns to his favorite hunting ground in Dortmund, locked in as the absolute number-one seed in form. His maximum-scoring frequency remains completely unmatched on the European circuit this season, ensuring he can easily blast anyone off the stage. The current double-digit market valuation represents pure betting leverage.

The Green Machine has picked up a couple of World Series events at the time of writing, and I fancy MVG could have another tilt at the World Championship. He is a multiple world champion and reached the final two years ago at Ally Pally. I am siding with Michael van Gerwen to go all the way to another world final.
["72% strike rate on Darts in the last 30 days","72% strike rate on Darts this month"]

Michael van Gerwen is the outright pick because major darts titles still tend to reward players who can live comfortably with expectation and keep producing under the brightest lights. When the tournament goes deep and the pressure sharpens, he remains one of the names most capable of owning that stage.

Rob Cross is showing signs of getting back to his old self, and the multiple major winner could make these odds look silly if he gets his TV game back before the end of the year. He is a previous winner, having won on debut in 2018, and in two of the last three World Championships it has been Luke Littler who has knocked him out. I think Cross could make a deep run in a major and maybe even win one in the next six months. If he does, he could go off as low as 20/1 to pick up his second World Championship.

Voltage is a former world champion, winning the title in 2018. He has also won the World Matchplay and European Championship. Rob Cross was a semi-finalist in 2024 and went to the fourth round last year. I am tipping, after some form in the Players Championship events and on the European Tour earlier this year, that Rob Cross looks a big price ahead of the World Championship at Ally Pally.

Beau Greaves is now a PDC title holder and looks set to further establish herself as a mainstay on the tour for years to come. Not only did she make history by winning the Players Championship 11, but she did so in spectacular fashion, beating three former PDC World champions in the quarter-final, semi-final, and final as she dispatched Rob Cross, Gary Anderson, and Michael Smith. As we speak now in April, she has a further eight months until the latter stages of the World Championship to get more stage and TV experience. If she can do that, she will make these odds look silly come December.

Bunting to finish top two makes strong sense because his controlled scoring rhythm, tournament temperament, and ability to raise his doubling level in long-format pressure matches give him the stability to navigate the deep rounds where volatility drops and experience becomes the decisive edge.
